key_insight: Gemini had the highest accuracy (90.29%), but SVM and the strongest transformer did not differ significantly, cautioning against claims of model-family superiority.
clinical_relevance: Classifying informal Bangla patient narratives could support specialty referral workflows, but clinical benefit and safety remain untested.
method: Compared 6 classical ML, 4 deep learning, 4 fine-tuned transformer, and 5 zero-shot LLM models.
Used 2,730 records across Medicine, Gynecology, Dermatology, Pediatrics, and Gastroenterology with a shared 80:20 train–test split.
Evaluated accuracy, macro-F1, and paired McNemar tests with Holm correction.
evidence_signal: Best-model accuracies were 90.29% for Gemini, 86.26% for XLM-RoBERTa, 84.98% for SVM, and 80.77% for Bidirectional GRU; the Gemini–Grok difference was not significant after correction.
watch_item: Evaluation covered only the five most represented specialties from a 20-specialty corpus, limiting generalizability to broader referral settings.
paper_title: Medical Specialty Prediction from Bangla Patient Narratives: A Comparative Study of ML, DL, Transformers, and LLMs
